claims.claim: Scalable, fine-grained three-stage data processing framework (document preparation, rule-based, model-based) for high-quality, diverse pretraining data
claims.quote: We propose a scalable and fine-grained three-stage data processing framework designed to generate large-scale, high-quality and diverse data for pretraining.

claims.claim: No synthetic data is used during pretraining
claims.quote: Notably, no synthetic data is used during pretraining.

claims.claim: 142B-total/14B-active MoE model achieving performance comparable to Qwen2.5-72B at reduced training and inference cost
claims.quote: We introduce dots.llm1, an open-source model that activates only 14B parameters during inference while delivering comprehensive and computationally efficient performance.

claims.claim: Innovative MoE all-to-all communication/computation overlap based on interleaved 1F1B pipeline scheduling and an efficient grouped GEMM implementation
claims.quote: we introduce an innovative MoE all-to-all communication and computation overlapping recipe based on 1F1B pipeline scheduling and an efficient grouped GEMM implementation to boost computational efficiency.

claims.claim: Open-sourcing intermediate training checkpoints every one trillion tokens
claims.quote: we open-source intermediate training checkpoints at every one trillion tokens, providing valuable insights into the learning dynamics of large language models.

rerun.quote: All models were evaluated within our internal framework under identical conditions.

scores_copied.quote: All models were evaluated within our internal framework under identical conditions.

data_disclosure.quote: During pre-training, we maintain a balanced 1:1 ratio of Chinese to English data, and no synthetic data is used.

tokens_disclosed.quote: We set the maximum sequence length to 8K during pre-training and train dots.llm1 on 11.2T tokens.

compute_disclosed.quote: if we consider the entire pretraining process, dots.llm1 requires only 1.46 million GPU hours, whereas Qwen2.5 72B consumes 6.12 million GPU hours

coding.note: I left out the architecture choices (QK-Norm, the auxiliary-loss-free balancing and FP32 gating). The paper attributes them to earlier work instead of claiming them as new, so there are no ARCH or TRAIN claims to check for ablations. I also didn't count the web clutter removal model and category balancing as separate claims. They appear only in Section 4.1, not the abstract or introduction, and the three-stage data framework claim already covers them. Two results look like evidence but were not used to code an ablation: the TxT360 web-data comparison on a 1.5B proxy model, and the grouped GEMM speed table against Transformer Engine. The comparators combine the base-model table (Table 2) and the instruct-model table (Table 5).
